query: What percentage of older patients should have frailty evaluated during healthcare encounters?
positive_chunk: [Discussion] Frailty assessments are increasingly recommended in clinical care. In Norway, recent publications have proposed implementing routine frailty assessments in emergency departments, and the European Joint Action on Frailty (ADVANTAGE) recommends evaluating frailty during all healthcare encounters involving older patients [24, 25]. Identifying pre-frail patients is crucial, as early interventions can prevent progression to frailty and reduce the risk of adverse outcomes during hospitalization. In this context, accurate classification of frailty serves primarily to inform clinical decision-making and risk stratification at the point of care.
hard_negative: Frailty assessments are crucial for determining the optimal dosage of medications in older adults with chronic conditions.

query: What is the prevalence of DDX41 variants in patients with MDS/AML?
positive_chunk: [Enrichment of DDX41 variants in MDS/AML (PS4)] To understand the prevalence of DDX41 variants across different disease contexts, we included a subset of patients from the DDX41-ASC with a diagnosis of MDS/AML (n = 34051), other myeloid neoplasms (n = 8072), unexplained cytopenias (n = 5156), and lymphoid neoplasms (n = 1228); 5179 individuals with aplastic anemia or unspecified hematologic malignancies were excluded. Among the 1594 cases with a germline DDX41 variant, we excluded 17 with aplastic anemia or healthy carriers, along with four cases with unclassified variants due to missing information, leaving 1573 cases included in the analysis.
hard_negative: DDX41 variants are commonly found in patients with solid tumors, which has significant implications for cancer treatment strategies.

query: What percentage of MDS/AML cases with germline DDX41 variants have single recurrent missense somatic variants?
positive_chunk: [Odds of pathogenicity from somatic DDX41 variants (PP4)] After observing a strong non-random association between germline and somatic DDX41 variants and building on previous work [3], we sought to evaluate the pathogenicity of germline DDX41 variants informed by the presence, number, and pattern of somatic variants. In cases of MDS/AML, the three most common pathogenic variants (c.3G>A, D140fs, and A500fs) were observed to have single recurrent missense (both R525H and non-R525H), single non-recurrent, and multiple somatic variants in 58%, 10%, and 0.7% of cases, respectively (Fig. 3E). In contrast, these somatic patterns were observed in 0.23%, 0.20%, and 0.14% of cases without a germline DDX41 variant (Fig. 3B)
hard_negative: The presence of somatic DDX41 variants is associated with a higher risk of developing leukemia in patients with germline variants.
